diff2ai.text: The retry-count purge in the SMS cron job deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of method, affecting EMAIL, WHATSAPP, and other reminder types
The retryCount > 1 branch ignores scheduled state, potentially removing reminders that were later scheduled successfully along with their referenceId, breaking later cancellation
The prisma.workflowReminder.update inside the catch block can throw and abort the entire loop, skipping all remaining reminders for the run
Using reminder.retryCount + 1 instead of atomic increment causes lost increments when cron invocations overlap or the same reminder is processed twice
Unindexed retryCount predicate in OR delete causes sequential scan of entire WorkflowReminder table on every cron invocation
Reminders are silently deleted after retries are exhausted with no logging or failure marking, so attendees never get SMS and there's no trace of why
The retry threshold of 1 is a magic number and with gt: 1 the reminder only gets 2 attempts which may not match intent

updateManyByCredentialId passes an empty data object and relies on Prisma's @updatedAt to bump the timestamp, but Prisma only sets @updatedAt when it actually runs an update - with empty data it may run no update at all, so SelectedCalendar.updatedAt never changes

The updateManyByCredentialId call adds an extra DB round-trip to every webhook-triggered cache refresh in the hot path of fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache, and a failure there makes the whole refresh reject after the cache was already written
The UI reads CalendarCache.updatedAt via cacheUpdatedAt, not SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, so the write to SelectedCalendar appears to have no consumer

Throwing plain Error instead of TRPCError in deleteCache handler surfaces as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500), hiding normal authorization or not-found outcomes as server faults and polluting error monitoring

Delete cached data action is offered for delegation credentials and team-owned credentials, but the handler only accepts credentials where userId === user.id, so for delegation credentials the delete action always fails with an error toast
Cache timestamp is formatted with hard-coded 'en-US' locale while the label is translated, causing non-US users to see ambiguous US date ordering (M/D/YY)
The handler always instantiates concrete CalendarCacheRepository instead of using the flag-aware factory, causing groupBy queries to run even when calendar-cache feature is disabled
sed -i '' in test-gcal-webhooks.sh only works with BSD/macOS sed, failing on GNU sed (Linux/CI)
ENV_FILE='../.env' resolves against caller's current directory instead of script's location, potentially writing to wrong file or creating stray .env outside repo
cleanup function in test-gcal-webhooks.sh always exits 0 even on failure paths, so callers cannot detect failure
When reusing already-running tmole, the URL comes from /tmp/tmole.log which may be missing or stale
npx tsx fetches undeclared dependency at runtime if tsx is not in devDependencies, making dev tooling non-reproducible and requiring network access
Migration contains misleading auto-generated comment saying column is added without default value when SQL actually uses DEFAULT NOW()
unsubscribe_link interpolates %{unsubscribe_url} but other mailers that set add_unsubscribe_link (like digests) do not pass it, causing I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and failing to send emails
TopicUser.find_by returns nil when user has no topic_users row for the topic, causing NoMethodError on tu.notification_level when clicking the email unsubscribe link

Unsubscribe action changes notification state on a plain GET request which is not idempotent - first hit drops to Regular, second hit drops to Muted, and lacks CSRF protection allowing silent topic muting via embedded images
tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change which publishes notification_level_change on MessageBus, causing other open tabs to show stale notification state

Confirmation text always says 'You will stop receiving notifications' but Tracking/Watching only lowers to Regular where users still get notified for replies and mentions, making the message misleading
Feed URL is not escaped before building HTML, allowing stored XSS via URLs containing special characters like quotes or angle brackets
Article body from feeds is stored and rendered as unsanitized HTML, allowing script injection from feed content
Kernel#open with user-influenced strings can execute shell commands (strings starting with |) or read local files
No timeout or size limit on remote fetches, allowing slow or huge responses to hang Sidekiq jobs
Feed items without content field cause NoMethodError when calling nil.scrub, aborting the entire poll
ERB template has invalid 'end if' syntax with no condition, causing incorrect template behavior
Unthrottled job enqueue on embed requests allows flooding Sidekiq with arbitrary embed_url values
Throttle key uses non-atomic setnx followed by expire, risking permanent key lock if process dies between calls
Missing guard for nil post when updating existing embed causes PostRevisor to raise on hard-deleted posts
Protocol-relative URLs starting with // are incorrectly rewritten by absolutize_urls, breaking images and links
Origin check uses substring match instead of exact comparison, accepting prefix-matching origins
Embed view crashes with 500 error when post's user is nil (deleted users)
Migration with force: true silently drops existing table, risking data loss on rerun or rollback
Disqus import lost category option and original created_at, causing topics to be uncategorized with wrong timestamps
Controller spec expects TopicRetriever but controller enqueues a job, test may not work correctly

useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities which hard-codes isFederated = false, causing federated Mimir rule groups to incorrectly get Update, Delete and Pause abilities when they should be treated as immutable

GrafanaRuleListItem in FilterView is missing the key prop that was present on the previous GrafanaRuleLoader, causing React key warnings and potential state attachment to wrong rules when filtered list changes

Pause/Restore/Export abilities are gated on prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule instead of prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule, causing Grafana-managed recording rules to lose pause, restore and export capabilities

canPause and canDelete can be true from Prom-only abilities but the list view no longer passes rulerRule, and the test asserts exactly 4 menu items hiding that Delete and Pause actions are missing for permitted users
isProvisionedPromRule reads promRule.provenance but no backend change ensures the Prometheus API returns this field, potentially making provisioned rules appear mutable in the list view
The returnTo parameter was dropped from the rule view link, causing navigation from list to rule detail and back to lose filter and scroll context
AlertRuleMenu passes a new array literal of actions on every render, making the useMemo ineffective since it depends on that array reference
Every list item runs both ruler and Prom ability computations including useFolder and useIsRuleEditable, adding unnecessary work on large lists when no rulerRule is provided
enableSqlExpressions returns false on both branches, making the FlagSqlExpressions check have no effect - the local variable 'enabled' holds the negated flag value making the code misleading
The code still calls h.features.IsEnabledGlobally() which adds a possible nil-pointer panic if features can be nil, for no benefit since the flag check doesn't work
Anyone who turns the flag on will still get 'not implemented' with nothing in the code explaining why

The new gate only lives in ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery but SQL expression nodes can also be built through the legacy pipeline (nodes.go → UnmarshalSQLCommand → sql.TablesList) which doesn't go through this reader
On the legacy path, TablesList now always fails with a generic 'not implemented' from the stub DB.RunCommands, giving users an opaque error instead of a clear 'disabled' message
TablesList and QueryFramesInto now always return errors, so existing tests that exercise real parsing or execution will fail but none are updated in this change
Tests should be skipped with a reason or changed to assert the disabled behaviour to keep CI green
TablesList still escapes quotes by hand and builds a DuckDB-specific json_serialize_sql statement then sends it to a stub that always errors - dead code left behind
The new DB type has no doc comment saying it is a placeholder, so future readers may assume it is a working in-memory engine
The string-interpolated SQL pattern in TablesList carries injection risk if the escaping is ever relied upon with a real engine
The isAccessTokenId matcher uses wrong substring indices (3-5 instead of 4-6) to extract the grant shortcut, returning 'ta' instead of the expected value for 'onrtac'
The isAccessTokenId matcher condition is inverted, returning false when the shortcut matches the expected value instead of when it doesn't match
The isAccessTokenId matcher does not verify that the prefix is exactly 6 characters long
Null check validates grantType twice instead of rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId to be accepted and produce token IDs like 'onrtac:null'
Grant shortcuts are not validated for length - a custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory returning a 3-letter shortcut produces token IDs that getTokenContextFromTokenId rejects
Grant shortcuts containing a colon break parsing of the ':' separator in token IDs
Null grant shortcut causes NPE in ConcurrentHashMap.put during postInit, blocking server startup
Grant shortcut collision with 'na' is not clearly reported
The new getShortcut() method is abstract with no default, causing existing third-party grant factories to fail to compile or link with AbstractMethodError
getShouldUseLightweightToken reads session.getContext().getClient() which may be null in admin or internal token generation paths, causing NPE
In token exchange flows, the context client can differ from the client the token is issued to, causing the encoded lightweight/regular flag to be wrong
Public Context copy constructor was removed without deprecation, breaking code that clones a Context
Main Context constructor calls formParams.getFirst() unconditionally, causing NPE when null formParams is passed
grantType is captured once in constructor and not recomputed in setFormParams, becoming stale if form params are replaced
UsernameForm calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments but the method signature requires a UserModel user parameter, causing compilation failure
isConditionalPasskeysEnabled returns false when user is null, which prevents conditional passkeys UI from showing on the initial login page for unidentified users, breaking normal passkey login flow

During re-authentication, any discoverable passkey can be presented because allowCredentials is not restricted - need to verify that action() rejects credentials whose user differs from the pre-set context user
Missing @Override annotation on shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators override method, which could cause silent failures if base signature changes

USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH constant was made public to allow AuthenticatorUtils to import it, creating an inappropriate dependency from util package to browser authenticator class and expanding public API surface
Test uses try/fail/catch(Exception) pattern instead of assertThrows, which could silently pass on unrelated failures like stale element or WebDriver errors
Test comment at line 304 incorrectly states passkeys are hidden because user does not have passkey, when actual reason is passkeys are disabled for the realm

queued: datetime = timezone.now() runs once at module import, causing all AssignmentSource instances without explicit queued to share the same timestamp instead of getting the time they were actually queued
to_dict() returns a raw datetime for queued which is not JSON-serializable, causing failures or incorrect coercion when passed as Celery task kwargs with JSON serializer
from_dict() does no type conversion, so a round-tripped queued arrives as a string instead of datetime

The abstract sync_assignee_outbound signature was not updated to accept assignment_source parameter, but the task calls it with that argument - concrete implementations without **kwargs or assignment_source parameter will raise TypeError
sync_status_outbound was changed to accept assignment_source but nothing in the diff passes that parameter to it, suggesting wrong method was modified

When assignment_source_dict fails to parse, from_dict returns None with no logging, causing should_sync to treat the assignment as having no source and potentially recreating the sync cycle the PR is meant to prevent
Subclass overrides of should_sync with the old one-argument signature will raise TypeError since the task now calls it with a second positional argument

MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated because it subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing required abstract methods (get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data), causing TypeError when detector_handler tries to instantiate it
evaluate docstring still says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult but the method now returns dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]

Tests cannot detect wrong value being passed to occurrence hook because build_mock_occurrence_and_event ignores the value parameter, so tests pass with value=6 even when evaluated values differ (10, 100, 8)
